name: Basilica of St. Mary of the Assumption
history: The first Mass in what is now Marietta was celebrated by Jesuit Joseph de Bonnecamp, chaplain to a French expedition from Quebec, where the Muskingum meets the Ohio River. Bishop John B. Purcell bought land in 1837 and sent a resident priest in 1838. Work on the present church began on 1 July 1903 and it was consecrated on 12 December 1909. It became a basilica in 2013.
arch: Spanish Colonial Revival by Cleveland architect Emile M. Uhlrich, with twin domed towers.
features: Its stained glass windows were made in Munich.
It belongs to the Diocese of Steubenville.

look.d: Twin towers with copper cupolas over Marietta, Ohio's first town.
The first Mass here was said where two rivers meet.

fun: Marietta was the first permanent American settlement in the Northwest Territory.
journal: Spanish domes in Ohio's oldest town. The rivers meet just down the hill.

quiz.q: Who celebrated the first Mass at Marietta?
